column9: Oct 2018 evidence: district 1:1 in grades 6-12 and expanding to K-12 later that year; Oakville Elem delivery completed K-12 milestone; COVID spring 2020 drive-thru distribution shows existing program
Connected Nation article: director started in 2014 with no 1:1; district achieved 1:1 take-home device benchmark during 2017-18 school year
Dyknow case study published Aug 2019 references established 1:1 Chromebook program; student newspaper article Nov 2018 confirms 1:1 Chromebook use; launch year not precisely documented

Tulsa World article Aug 20 2014: district bought 850 Chromebooks for all freshmen in pilot; following year ~2500 more for remaining HS grades; bond issue $12.8M incl $4.3M tech; later expanded to gr 3-12
District has Chromebook G Suite program confirmed; no dated launch source found; Chromebook handbook and agreement forms exist but year of initiation undocumented
Daily Herald 9/28/2015: board approved ~2180 Chromebook lease for Woodland Middle School for 2016-17 school year; part of 'Woodland Inspires' initiative; gr 4-8 eventually 1:1
Chromebook agreement documented for 2020-21 school year at Tecumseh HS; students grades 6-12 issued Lenovo Chromebooks; K-2 login also referenced; no earlier firm-year source found

District confirmed 1:1 Chromebooks gr 1-12; 2014 Measure I bond ($175.9M) included technology upgrades; no specific year for Chromebook rollout found; COVID-era shift confirmed as major expansion point
District provided Chromebooks for 2020-21 SY with both face-to-face and virtual options; COVID-era rollout; Chromebook device agreement in student handbook; no pre-2020 launch evidence found
Every Monroe City School student has assigned Chromebook; district lauded for tech-based distance learning during COVID; no pre-2020 firm launch date found

Chromebook distribution drive-thru events documented 2020-21; EdSurge profile notes district 'not yet at 1:1 ratio' but schools 'very close'; COVID-era distribution via Senator Archuleta event Aug 2021
WCPO article: 2020-21 started with 2530 laptops for grades 9-12; phased rollout district-wide by 2024; every student personal laptop
LanSchool/district case study: began 2013 testing; launched 1:1 personal Chromebooks for all gr 5-12 students in 2015-16 school year; had 1:1 program before COVID; later K-4 added
District has technology department and Chromebook programs referenced; Governor Abbott/AT&T delivered 150 laptops to seniors (2026); no 1:1 district-wide program year found
Chromebook agreement form documented for 2022-23; district has tech department and confirmed Chromebook program; no firm pre-2020 launch source found; upper bound from existence of 2022-23 agreement
2015 technology-only bond passed for 1:1 Chromebooks for ~8100 students in gr 3-12; implementation began after bond; $7.98M issued 2016; devices kept ~5 years; K-2 expanded 2020-21
Georgetown County School District confirmed Chromebook use via IT department; 212 degree initiative references gr 2-12 achievement program; no 1:1 device launch year found
Santa Rosa City Schools (same location, Ridgway Ave) shifted to 1:1 Chromebooks during COVID; Superintendent purchased 3000 Chromebooks Mar 2020 for distance learning; COVID-era expansion confirmed
District uses Chromebooks for students (login instructions documented); COVID-era expansion referenced; no pre-2020 firm date found; Chromebook distribution confirmed but no launch year
District confirms 1:1 technology with both iPads and Google Chromebooks for every student; no specific launch year documented in available sources; ESSER funding used post-2020

Conway Public Schools has Chromebook use agreement and student technology program; @conwayschools.info gmail for Chromebooks; protection plan started 2022-23 for gr 8-12; no district-wide 1:1 launch year found
District issues iPads (PK-5) and HP Chromebooks (6-12) with cases; $35 annual tech fee for gr 6-12; 1:1 Learning FAQ page on district site; no firm launch year documented

District purchases both HP Chromebooks and Apple iPads for students; technology sustainability plan replacing devices 6+ years old; no 1:1 launch year documented; student/parent device handbook agreement in place
NJ Patch article: district sent home 5000 Chromebooks for COVID remote learning; allowed families to keep them over summer 2020; pandemic-driven 1:1 for all K-8 students
PinalCentral Dec 18 2016: district provided all K-12 students with iPads via 3-year Apple lease; ~2500 devices; gr 7-12 take-home with $50 annual fee; elementary stay at school
